subtopic: Equation of a straight line (y = mx + c)
title: Equation of a straight line (y = mx + c)
subtitle: Straight-Line Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can identify and write the equation of a straight line in the form y = mx + c.

key_vocab.definition: Every straight line can be written as y = mx + c, where m is the gradient (slope) and c is the y-intercept.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can identify and write the equation of a straight line in the form y = mx + c.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: y = mx + c -- Every straight line can be written as y = mx + c, where m is the gradient (slope) and c is the y-intercept.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
In y = mx + c, m is the gradient (how steep) and c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
y = mx + c
m = gradient, c = y-intercept

Key examples:
  ✓ y = 2x + 3 has gradient 2 and y-intercept 3  (m = 2, c = 3)
  ✓ y = -x + 5 has gradient -1  (line slopes downward)
  ✓ y = &frac{1}{2}x has gradient &frac{1}{2} and y-intercept 0  (passes through origin)
  ✗ y = 3x + 2 has gradient 2  (gradient is 3, not 2)
  ✗ y = 4 - 2x has positive gradient  (gradient is -2 (negative))

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – identifying m and c
  State the gradient and y-intercept of y = 3x - 2.
  Compare with y = mx + c
  m = 3 (gradient)
  c = -2 (y-intercept)
  Gradient = 3, y-intercept = -2
  (Read m and c directly from the equation.)

Example 2 – writing the equation
  A line has gradient 4 and y-intercept -1. Write its equation.
  Use y = mx + c
  Substitute m = 4 and c = -1
  y = 4x - 1
  y = 4x - 1
  (Plug the gradient and y-intercept into the formula.)

sections.title: Identifying gradient and y-intercept
sections.content:
State m and c for each equation.

(a) y = 5x + 2
(b) y = -3x + 1
(c) y = &frac{1}{2}x - 4
(d) y = x

sections.title: Writing equations
sections.content:
Write the equation y = mx + c.

(a) Gradient 2, y-intercept 5
(b) Gradient -1, y-intercept 3
(c) Gradient &frac{3}{4}, y-intercept -2
(d) Gradient 0, y-intercept 6

sections.title: Rearranging equations
sections.content:
Write in the form y = mx + c.

(a) 3x + y = 10
(b) 2y = 6x - 4
(c) x + 2y = 8
(d) 4x - 2y = 6

sections.title: From two points
sections.content:
Find the equation of the line through these points.

(a) (0, 1) and (2, 5)
(b) (0, -3) and (3, 6)
(c) (1, 4) and (3, 10)
(d) (2, 1) and (6, 9)

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Line passes through (0, 4) with gradient -2. Equation?
(b) Which line is steeper: y = 3x + 1 or y = 5x - 2?
(c) Does (2, 7) lie on y = 3x + 1?
(d) Find where y = 2x - 1 crosses the x-axis.
(e) Write 6x + 3y = 9 in y = mx + c form.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept
✗ y = 3x + 2 has y-intercept 3
✓ A line with gradient 0 is horizontal
✗ y = 5 - 2x has a positive gradient
✓ The y-intercept is found by setting x = 0

Mixed problems:
